item.title: Would love some logo feedback (also looking to hire designer for touch ups)
item.description:
Here’s the logo and some additional information: http://i.imgur.com/90M7zzt.png

For those interested in the job (contact me at cwrichardkim@gmail.com):
The Old
We find that our current logo has a range of issues:

  1. It’s too bland. We strived for simple, but ended up with bland.
  2. Unrelatable to our primary audience (college students)
  3. We strove for: Sleek, high quality, class, professional, fun

The New
We’re looking for a new identity for our upcoming expansion

  1. Color scheme. Finding a color scheme that fits us is our primary mission. The colors have to work across the platform
  2. More fun while keeping the quality. Our userbase consists primarily of college students looking for a pizza deal and an upcoming concert. We’re looking for a way to keep the sleek and simple image but add a splash of personality
  3. Minimal changes to the current logo. We still want our image to be continuous and recognizable after the change
  4. Adjectives: Sleek, simple, fun, reliable, likable, lighthearted, going out

item.title: Luis Siquot
item.description: Luis Siquot was born in 1945 in Neuquén. While working as graphic designer between 1964 and 1968 he studied cinema, architecture, and modern literature in Córdoba, Argentina. During that time he won several first prizes in design contests. In 1965 he moved for one year to São Paulo, Brazil, to work at the Editôra Abril where he learned magazine design. In 1967 he was awarded a scholarship to study at the HfG Ulm by the German DAAD, but unfortunately the school was closed in 1968.

item.title: David Brezina
item.description:
Indices : Designers : David Březina

Czech type designer and typographer, writer, lecturer, the impresario of TypeTalks, and partner at Rosetta Type Foundry. He got Masters degrees in Informatics (Masaryk University, Brno) and Typeface Design ( University of Reading, UK). From 2004 to 2007 he also ran his own design studio, with projects in graphic, web, and interface design. He has been working as an associate with Tiro Typeworks and giving various type workshops around Europe.

item.title: Dino dos Santos
item.description: DSType was founded in late 1994 by Dino dos Santos and since then designed typefaces for several corporations, magazines and cultural projects. Graduated in Graphic Design by ESAD, Matosinhos in 1994, in 2002 was awarded with an MA in Multimedia Arts at FBAUP, Porto, with a thesis on Digital Typography in Multimedia Environments. Teaches Typographic Studies at ESAD-Matosinhos. DSType’s work is featured in several magazines like Computer Arts (UK), Creative Review (UK), Page (DE), Publish (PT), Page (PT), ZOOT (UK / PT), among others. Designed some notable typefaces like ANDRADE, winner of the Creative Review Type Design Awards, for the Best Revival; VENTURA, awarded with the Certificate of Excellence in Type Design by the Type Directors Club of New York; ESTA (Best Serif Font of 2005 for MyFonts and Favorite Fonts of 2006 for Typographica); ESTILO (Favorite Fonts of 2006 for Typographica); ESTILO SCRIPT (Best Script Font of 2006 for MyFonts); LEITURA (Top 10 Fonts of 2007 for MyFonts, Favorite Fonts of 2007 for Typographica and Silver Award by Clube de Criativos de Portugal). Contributes regularly to conferences, seminars and publications.

item.description:

item.title: Michael Abbink
item.description:
Indices : Designers : Michael Abbink

Mr. Abbink left Wolff Olins (NYC) in June 2006 after 3 years and is now trying his hand at freelance and developing his own design practice. He was co-founder and creative director of Method, a design firm based in San Francisco doing graphic design, and web & interface design. He formerly worked at Meta Design and Apple Computer, and is the designer of FF Kievit and FF Milo typeface families.

item.title: Nick Cooke
item.description:
Indices : Designers : Nick Cooke

Nick Cooke started his typographic journey as a lettering artist, in London, in 1982, crafting type by hand for book jackets. Working with David Cox (the great nephew of Eric Gill) was for him an apprenticeship into acquiring an appreciation of letterforms and proportions.

Involved in the digital type eversince computers made it to the mainline, he began to experiment with designing complete typefaces using Fontographer. His first type family ‘Penguin’, developed while working for Prima magazine, was accepted by Fontshop International in 1995. His second type family, an one-off script font ‘ITC Dartangnon’ was produced in a similar manner at his next place of employment.

item.title: Matthew Carter
item.description:
Indices : Designers : Matthew Carter

Born: United Kingdom, 1937.

Son of Harry Carter, Royal Designer for Industry, contemporary British type designer and ultimate craftsman, trained as a punchcutter at Enschedé by Paul Rädisch, responsible for Crosfield’s typographic program in the early 1960s, Mergenthaler Linotype’s house designer 1965–1981.

Carter is a prolific designer who has produced many successful and significant faces in his career such as Olympian, Bell Centennial, Galliard, Charter and Miller (in chronological order).

He has in recent years designed Verdana, Tahoma and Georgia for Microsoft; these fonts are tuned to be extremely legible even at very small sizes on the screen.

item.title: Calvin Glenn
item.description:
Indices: Designers: Calvin Glenn

Founder of NIMX and designer of several typefaces including the popular Jacoby family. Jacoby had the distinction of being one of the earliest (if not very first) commercial third-party Multiple Master typefaces. Calvin is currently Marketing Manager at Oracle.

item.title: James Grieshaber
item.description:
Indices : Designers : James Grieshaber

James Grieshaber attended Rochester Institute of Technology and earned a BFA in Graphic Design. Grieshaber was a staff designer at P22 Type Foundry and helped establish International House of Fonts. He has been honored with awards of Excellence in Type Design from Association Typographique International (ATypI) for Gothic Gothic and from TypeArt'05 for his Operina Cyrillic type designs. He has been involved with the Society of Typographic Aficionados and served as Chairman of SOTA from 2008—2010. Designer and Co-editor of the Indie Fonts book series, Grieshaber has taught typography at RIT and now runs Typeco, his own type design studio, in Chicago, IL.

item.title: Dan Reynolds
item.description:
Indices : Designers : Dan Reynolds

Born in Baltimore in 1979, Dan studied Graphic Design at RISD before moving to Europe. In 2004, Dan co-founded the Offenbach Typostammtisch during a brief stint as a graduate student at the HfG Offenbach. Later, he studied on the University of Reading MA Type Design course, where he graduated as part of the class of 2008. Dan teaches typography and type design courses at several German design schools, and works as a type designer in Berlin

item.title: Education
item.description:
Indices: Education

Type design (strictly)

  • MA Typeface Design
  • Type & Media (1-year postgraduate course) at KABK, Den Haag, The Netherlands
    Teachers: Jan Willem Stas, Erik van Blokland, Peter Verheul, Frank Blokland, Petr van Blokland, Françoise Berserik, Peter Bilak, Robin Kinross, Paul van der Laan, Frans van Mourik, Christoph Noordzij, Just van Rossum, Fred Smeijers
    Language: English
  • Carrera de Diseño de Tipografía (CDT-UBA) (1 and a half-year postgraduate course) at Universidad de Buenos Aires (UBA), Buenos Aires, Argentina
    Director: Rubén Fontana. Academic coordinator: Marcela Romero. Teachers: Carlos Carpintero, Miguel Catopodis, Pablo Cosgaya, Aldo De Losa, Griselda Flesler, Ruben Fontana, Tomás García Ferrari, Víctor García, Patricio Gatti, Horacio Gorodischer, Alejandro Lo Celso, Darío Muhafara, Betina Naab, Alejandro Paul, Mariana Podetti, María Eugenia Roballos, Eduardo Tunni, Marcela Romero, José Scaglione, Andrés Torresi.
    Language: Spanish
  • The Type@Cooper certificate programs at the Cooper Union in New York City. Language: English
  • Certificate of Advanced Studies (CAS) Type Design at Hochschule der Künste, Zürich, Switzerland. 1-year part-time program.
  • Master of Advanced Studies (MAS) in Type Design and Typography at Hochschule der Künste, Zürich, Switzerland. 2-year part-time program.
    Teachers: Hans-Jürg Hunziker, André Baldinger, Rudolf Barmettler; guest lecturers have included Hans Eduard Meier, Robin Kinross, Fred Smeijers, Gerard Unger, Erik van Blokland, Jeremy Tankard, Bruno Maag, Luc(as) de Groot, Ole Schäfer, Peter Bilak
    Language: German (plus some French & English)
  • ‘DSAA Création Typographique’ (2-year program) at Ecole Estienne, Paris, France
    Language: French
  • 3-year Bachelor program in Type Design & 1-year ‘Meisterschüler’ program at Hochschule für Grafik und Buchkunst/Academy of Visual Arts in Leipzig, Germany
    Supervised by Fred Smeijers
    Language: German (English?)
  • Master’s degree at Centro de Estudios Gestalt, Veracruz, Mexico
    Language: Spanish
  • Non-academic: Font Bureau Operated by Berlow and others in Boston, USA, with design collaborators including Roger Black, Cyrus Highsmith, Jill Pichotta, and others, as suggested by Paul

See also: Studying type design by Luc Devroye.
